_comment: OpenSSF Best Practices answers for the passing and silver levels, read from this file by bestpractices.dev. Every claim here is verifiable from this repository or from a dated measurement recorded in the justification; where a criterion is not met it says so and points at the issue that tracks closing it, rather than being argued around. Gold is not answered here: three of its criteria (bus_factor, contributors_unassociated, two_person_review) need a second maintainer — see GOVERNANCE.md and docs/ROADMAP.md.
description_good_justification: The README's opening states the problem in user-facing terms (an agent asked to change a function hallucinates a renamed symbol, edits the wrong community, or breaks a call chain three modules away, because agents operate on strings while codebases have structure) and then the solution. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline#readme
interact_justification: Obtain and use: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline#getting-started. Give feedback: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues. Contribute: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md documents how to contribute: dev setup, branch naming, the pull-request workflow, the coding standard, the mandatory testing policy, and what not to do.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards-excerpt states the required standard (rustfmt plus the zetetic coding standards, with the project-specific rules spelled out), and https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#testing-policy-mandatory states the acceptance requirements for tests.
license_location_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/LICENSE in the standard top-level location, and Cargo.toml declares license = "MIT": https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/Cargo.toml
documentation_basics_justification: The README documents what the software is, how to build and register it, the 26 MCP tools, the 10 pipeline stages, the architecture and the storage model: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline#readme. The per-stage specification lives in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/tree/main/stages and the stage-to-tool map in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/NOTES.md
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the MCP tool surface. All 26 tools, their inputs and their outputs are documented at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline#26-mcp-tools, and the machine-readable JSON Schemas that the server advertises are in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/src/tool_schemas.rs
sites_https_justification: Project site, repository and release downloads are GitHub, HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests: searchable, each message addressable by URL, open to new participants, no proprietary client needed. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues
english_justification: All documentation, issues, commit messages and code comments are in English.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: commits on main through 2026-07-27, releases through v0.8.2 (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/releases), and 62 of the 63 issues opened to date are closed.
repo_track_justification: Git, with the full history public since the first commit.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands through a pull request against main, and main is protected against direct pushes, force pushes and deletion, so interim work is visible as PR branches rather than squashed away. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/pulls?q=is%3Apr
repo_distributed_justification: Git is a distributed version control system; any clone is a complete copy of the history.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique semantic version, carried identically by four manifests (Cargo.toml, server.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json) and checked by https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/scripts/check_marketplace_pins.py in CI, so a version cannot be released while the manifests disagree. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/releases
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning, stated in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and applied to every tag (v0.5.0 through v0.8.2).
version_tags_justification: Every release is a git tag: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/tags
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md, Keep a Changelog format, one section per release, with the reasoning and the issue numbers for each change. Also published on each GitHub release: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release to date has fixed a publicly known vulnerability with a CVE assignment, so there is none to name in the notes. The one RUSTSEC advisory present in the dependency tree (RUSTSEC-2026-0202, cxx 1.0.138) is `unsound`-class rather than a vulnerability, is not reachable from this code, and is blocked upstream by an exact pin — recorded with its evidence at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/deny.toml
report_process_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues with three templates (bug, feature, audit finding) at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/tree/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE, and the process described in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues, with structured templates for bug reports, enhancement requests and audit findings: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues
report_responses_justification: 62 of 63 issues opened to date are closed, and the recent ones were acknowledged and closed the same day or the next (for example #140, #141, #142, #143, #148, #153 and #155, all opened and closed on 2026-07-26 to 2026-07-27). One issue is open, the #151 file-size refactor epic. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests use the same tracker and the same response pattern, with a dedicated template (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.yml); each one raised so far was answered and resolved. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_archive_justification: Issues and pull requests are public and permanently archived: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/SECURITY.md documents the reporting process, what to include, the per-severity response SLA, and the coordinated-disclosure timeline.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private GitHub security advisories are enabled on the repository (verified via the GitHub API private-vulnerability-reporting endpoint, enabled=true, 2026-07-28), so the channel SECURITY.md names is actually open: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/security/advisories/new. SECURITY.md documents the process and the per-severity response SLA: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/SECURITY.md. Because that form is a GitHub feature a repository setting can switch off — which is exactly how this criterion came to be Unmet — SECURITY.md also names a fallback that does not depend on it, the address hello@ai-architect.tools, under the same SLA. No OpenPGP key is advertised: publishing one the maintainer cannot reliably decrypt with would be worse than plaintext.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability has been reported in the last 6 months, so there is no response time to report. The commitment (24 hours for critical, 3 days for high) is at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/SECURITY.md#response-sla
build_justification: `cargo build --release` builds the server from source with the toolchain pinned in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/rust-toolchain.toml. Documented at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline#clone--build
build_common_tools_justification: Cargo, the standard Rust build tool. No bespoke build system.
build_floss_tools_justification: The Rust toolchain, cargo, tree-sitter, tantivy and LadybugDB are all FLOSS; https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/deny.toml enforces a permissive-licence allowlist over the whole dependency graph.
test_justification: An automated test suite runs with `cargo test`: 947 tests passing, 0 failing, 2 ignored (measured 2026-07-28 on the pinned 1.95.0 toolchain). It covers every pipeline stage end to end plus the structural graph-accuracy gate. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/tree/main/tests
test_invocation_justification: `cargo test` — a single standard command, documented in the README and in CONTRIBUTING.md.
test_most_justification: 947 tests over the whole tool surface and every stage, with 81.56% line coverage measured 2026-07-28 (cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.7, `cargo llvm-cov --workspace`). The suite includes a structural accuracy gate with a ratcheting floor (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/tests/graph_accuracy.rs) rather than only example-based tests.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: Every push to main and every pull request runs the full suite, the graph-accuracy gate, clippy at -D warnings and rustfmt --check: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml. CodeQL, fuzzing and the supply-chain audit run alongside it.
test_policy_justification: The policy that new functionality ships with tests in the same pull request is written at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#testing-policy-mandatory
tests_are_added_justification: Enforced in review and visible in the tree: 34 test files carry the issue number of the defect or feature they cover in their header (for example tests/no_naive_cypher_escape.rs for #16, tests/coverage_honesty.rs for #57, tests/parser_parse_bound.rs for #148, tests/uses_edges_92.rs for #92).
tests_documented_added_justification: The requirement is documented for contributors at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#testing-policy-mandatory
warnings_justification: The Rust compiler's warnings are on by default and clippy runs workspace-wide over all targets: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are errors in CI — `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails the build on any warning, so none can accumulate. There are zero at HEAD.
warnings_strict_justification: Maximally strict and enforced, not merely enabled: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` plus `cargo fmt --all --check` run as a required status check on every push and pull request (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml, the clippy job). Allow-attributes require an inline justification per https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards-excerpt
know_secure_design_justification: The secure design principles applied here, and where each one lands in the code, are argued in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md (Claim 4): fail-safe defaults and allowlisting at the tool boundary, complete mediation at the single argument-parsing choke point, economy of mechanism, and least privilege in CI tokens.
know_common_errors_justification: Demonstrated rather than asserted: the Cypher injection class was found, fixed at the root with one escaping choke point, and then pinned mechanically so a third reintroduction fails `cargo test` (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/tests/no_naive_cypher_escape.rs). CodeQL runs the security-and-quality suite on every push and pull request, and the parser entry points are fuzzed under AddressSanitizer.
crypto_published_justification: The only algorithms used are SHA-256 (RustCrypto `sha2`, for the stage-2 transcript digest) and BLAKE3 (in crates/zera). Both are publicly published and expert-reviewed; nothing proprietary or unpublished is used.
crypto_call_justification: No cryptographic primitive is re-implemented. SHA-256 comes from the RustCrypto `sha2` crate and BLAKE3 from the `blake3` crate, both declared in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/Cargo.toml
crypto_floss_justification: `sha2` and `blake3` are MIT/Apache-2.0 FLOSS, and https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/deny.toml enforces a permissive-licence allowlist over the entire dependency graph.
crypto_keylength_justification: The software generates and uses no cryptographic keys. It is a local stdio MCP server with no authentication, no network communication and no key-based security mechanism, so there is no key length to configure.
crypto_working_justification: No default security mechanism depends on a cryptographic algorithm. SHA-256 is used as an integrity digest over a locally written transcript artifact and BLAKE3 for content addressing in the ZERA reference implementation; neither protects against an adversary. For completeness: no broken algorithm (MD5, SHA-1, RC4, DES) appears anywhere in the tree, checked 2026-07-27.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No security mechanism depends on cryptography, so there is no default algorithm choice whose weakening would matter. See the crypto_working justification for the two non-security hash uses.
crypto_pfs_justification: The software implements no network cryptographic protocol. It speaks MCP over stdio and opens no socket, so there is no key-agreement protocol that could offer forward secrecy.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software authenticates no users and stores no passwords. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/PRIVACY.md states that it collects and transmits nothing.
crypto_random_justification: No cryptographic keys, nonces or tokens are generated. Randomness is used only for non-security purposes such as test fixtures.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are distributed over HTTPS from GitHub, and every asset ships a published SHA-256 companion file retrieved over the same HTTPS channel: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/releases
delivery_unsigned_justification: No downloadable asset is published without an integrity value: each tarball and the .mcpb bundle has a matching .sha256 file on the release page, served over HTTPS. (The stronger property — a cryptographic signature over the artifact — is not yet true of a published release; that is reported honestly under signed_releases rather than claimed here.)
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known unpatched vulnerability. `cargo audit` and `cargo deny` run daily and block (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/supply-chain-audit.yml). The single accepted advisory entry, RUSTSEC-2026-0202, is `unsound`-class rather than a vulnerability, is unreachable from this code, and cannot be resolved from this repository because lbug pins cxx with an exact requirement — the evidence, including the checked lbug versions, is written into https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/deny.toml and tracked upstream as issue #110.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability is outstanding; the daily audit gate blocks a release path on any RUSTSEC advisory that is not explicitly accepted with a written reason.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is present in the repository. Scanned 2026-07-27 across every tracked file for AWS access-key ids, GitHub tokens, OpenAI keys, Slack tokens, PEM private-key headers and assigned secret literals: zero hits. The server itself asks for no credentials (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/PRIVACY.md). That scan was a snapshot; the standing control is GitHub's own secret scanning, enabled together with push protection on 2026-07-28 so a secret is blocked at push time rather than found afterwards. Verify: `gh api repos/cdeust/automatised-pipeline --jq '.security_and_analysis.secret_scanning.status'` and `.secret_scanning_push_protection.status` both return `enabled`. The first full-history scan raised zero alerts (`gh api repos/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/secret-scanning/alerts` returns an empty array).
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL analyses both the Rust source and the GitHub Actions workflows on every push, every pull request and weekly: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml. Clippy runs workspace-wide over all targets at -D warnings as a required check.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL runs with `queries: security-and-quality`, which includes the common-vulnerability query packs, over the rust and actions languages: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Zero open CodeQL alerts (checked 2026-07-27). The only CodeQL alert ever raised, rust/unused-variable, was dismissed as a false positive in the extractor's handling of inline format-args capture, and the dismissal is backed by an executable negative control in PR #118 rather than an assertion. The one open code-scanning alert is OpenSSF Scorecard's SAST posture score (9/10), which is a score, not a vulnerability.
static_analysis_often_justification: Every push to main and every pull request, plus a weekly scheduled run so a newly published query rule reaches the repository during a quiet period.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Two libFuzzer targets over the parser entry points run in CI: a 120-second smoke run on every pull request and a 900-second run nightly. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml and https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/tree/main/fuzz/fuzz_targets
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The fuzz targets run under AddressSanitizer: cargo-fuzz's --sanitizer option defaults to `address` (rust-fuzz/cargo-fuzz, src/options.rs) and the workflow does not override it. The fuzz profile also keeps debug-assertions and overflow-checks on (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/fuzz/Cargo.toml), so a violated invariant becomes a crash the fuzzer can find. This matters here because the parser runtime underneath is C.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Assertions are deliberately enabled in the dynamic-analysis run: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/fuzz/Cargo.toml sets debug-assertions = true and overflow-checks = true in the fuzz release profile, with the reason written in place — a panic is the signal being hunted, so optimising assertions away would defeat the harness.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The one defect dynamic analysis found is fixed and pinned: the OOM in the tree-sitter external scanner discovered by the parse_file target (issue #148) is bounded, with a regression test at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/tests/parser_parse_bound.rs. No finding is outstanding.
achieve_passing_justification: Every passing-level criterion above is now answered Met or N/A with evidence, with no exception. The last one outstanding was vulnerability_report_private: private security advisories are enabled, and SECURITY.md additionally names a channel that does not depend on that repository setting, so the documented process survives the setting being switched off again (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues/159, closed).
dco_justification: There is no DCO sign-off requirement and no CLA today. All non-trivial code to date is the sole maintainer's own, contributed under the project's MIT licence. The position, and the intent to adopt a DCO (`git commit -s`) rather than a CLA if outside contributors begin submitting non-trivial changes, is stated at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#contribution-licensing
governance_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md — who decides, how a decision is made, how disagreement is resolved, how a change gets in, and how someone becomes a maintainer.
code_of_conduct_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, in the standard top-level location, and linked from CONTRIBUTING.md.
roles_responsibilities_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities — maintainer, contributor and security reporter, what each is responsible for, and who holds the maintainer role. It states plainly that there is currently one person in it.
access_continuity_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity-of-access — what survives the maintainer becoming unavailable (public MIT source, complete history in every clone, tagged releases, a compiler and dependency graph pinned so a fork can rebuild the exact artifact), and what is genuinely single-owner. The single point of failure is named rather than papered over.
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1: one maintainer. This is stated rather than hidden, together with what survives their loss and how a fork continues, at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity-of-access. Adding a second maintainer is item 5 on https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md and is the single change that would most improve this project's resilience.
documentation_roadmap_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md states what the project intends to do over the next year (graph fidelity, the file-size split epic, making the supply-chain assurance real on a published release, holding coverage as a gate, and the badge levels) and has an explicit section on what it will not do — no code writing, no PRD generation, no network at index time, no model runtime.
documentation_architecture_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline#architecture documents the high-level design: the transport-to-handler-to-core layering, every core module and its responsibility, the graph-per-finding storage model and why it was chosen, and the address-space configuration with its measured derivation. The trust boundaries between those components are enumerated in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md
documentation_security_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/SECURITY.md states what a user can and cannot expect: exactly what the tool reads, what assurance is offered over the artifact, and the limits stated rather than implied. The argument that those requirements are met, with its trust boundaries and residual risks, is at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline#getting-started — prerequisites, clone and build, register the MCP server, and a first run that exercises the handshake over stdio, with a copy-pasteable JSON-RPC call.
documentation_current_justification: Documentation is corrected in the same pull request as the change, and version pins are machine-checked rather than hand-maintained (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/scripts/check_marketplace_pins.py runs in CI and fails on a stale pin). Numeric claims are no longer hand-maintained either: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/scripts/check_doc_claims.py runs in the required `cargo test` job and fails when the README's advertised tool count, tool names, language count, test count or coverage percentage disagrees with the tool registry, the Language enum, the suite's own tally or the coverage job, and when the repository-layout tree names a path that does not exist. It was written after drift was found by hand (an advertised 434 tests against a 947-test suite) and it immediately caught four more: 24 advertised tools against 26 registered, 10 languages against 11, 16 hidden tools against 18, and two registered tools that no section documented. All were fixed and the scale table was re-measured on the lbug version actually depended on, closing https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues/161.
documentation_achievements_justification: The repository front page identifies and hyperlinks its achievements as badges: the OpenSSF Best Practices badge for this project (https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/13845, live in the README badge row and linked back to the project page), alongside licence, test count, measured coverage, tool count and language count. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline#readme. Release-by-release achievements are recorded in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project results have no graphical user interface: the software is an MCP server speaking stdio, and its output is JSON and Markdown that the consuming host renders, so the host's own accessibility settings apply. The project site is GitHub, and the documentation is Markdown with text alternatives on its images (the README banner carries an alt attribute).
internationalization_justification: The software's user-facing strings — tool descriptions, error messages, diagnostics — are English literals and are not externalized for localization. The code it indexes is unaffected (identifiers and paths are passed through unchanged in whatever language the user writes, and ten source languages are supported), but the software itself has not been internationalized and is reported as such rather than claimed.
sites_password_security_justification: The project operates no site of its own that authenticates external users. The repository, the issue tracker and the release downloads are hosted on GitHub, and the software stores no passwords for inbound authentication.
maintenance_or_update_justification: The support policy is stated at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/SECURITY.md — the latest minor release on main receives security patches. The upgrade path is a reinstall (`cargo install ai-architect-mcp`, a new release tarball, or the plugin pin moving), and there is no user-authored persisted state to migrate: graph artifacts are derived data, regenerated by re-indexing. Breaking changes are recorded per release in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability has been reported and resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit. The standing commitment to credit reporters in the release notes for the patched version, unless they request anonymity, is at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/SECURITY.md#recognition
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/SECURITY.md#response-sla documents the response process: a per-severity first-response and patch SLA, and a five-step coordinated-disclosure timeline from private report to public advisory, including the default 30-day disclosure window and reporter credit.
coding_standards_justification: The primary language is Rust; the standard is rustfmt plus the project-specific rules named at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards-excerpt, which cites the full zetetic coding standards it derives from (no warnings, no unjustified unwrap/expect, no unsafe without a safety comment, sourced constants, file and function size caps, Result over panics at API boundaries).
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Automatically enforced by two FLOSS tools as required status checks on every push and pull request: `cargo fmt --all --check` for formatting and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` for the lint rules (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml). Exceptions must be a single #[allow(...)] with an inline justification, per CONTRIBUTING.md.
build_standard_variables_justification: Native binaries are produced, and the standard variables are honoured rather than replaced. Cargo passes RUSTFLAGS through to rustc, and the C/C++ dependencies (the tree-sitter runtime, zstd, the LadybugDB core) build through the `cc` crate, which reads CC, CFLAGS, CXX and CXXFLAGS. Nothing in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.cargo/config.toml or the workflows overrides them — the release job only adds ZSTD_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG, which extends the build environment rather than replacing a user-provided value.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Debugging information is controlled by the Cargo profile and honoured by `cargo build` and `cargo install`, which is how a developer or packager builds this project; nothing in the build system discards it. Disclosure: the release workflow runs a best-effort `strip` on the packaged tarball binary for download size (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml), so the prebuilt artifact is stripped. A user who needs symbols builds from source with the toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml and gets an identical binary — see build_repeatable.
build_non_recursive_justification: One Cargo workspace with a single, accurate dependency graph across all six members (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/Cargo.toml). Cargo resolves cross-member dependencies itself; there is no recursive make and no per-subdirectory independent build.
build_repeatable_justification: Measured, not assumed. The compiler is pinned in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/rust-toolchain.toml (1.95.0) and the dependency graph in Cargo.lock. On 2026-07-27 (macOS aarch64, rustc 1.95.0), `cargo build --release --bin automatised-pipeline` produced sha256 5b3dcc46f4dc2fcbd0969fa1b27ff75ce576b75ce2e833a9aee8977246df8650; the target directory was then deleted and the build repeated from scratch, producing the identical digest. Stated limit: the target path is embedded, so a build into a different CARGO_TARGET_DIR differs (389394362d5e...); bit-identity across different paths would additionally require --remap-path-prefix, which is not configured today.
installation_common_justification: Three commonly-used conventions, all documented at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline#getting-started: the language package manager (`cargo install ai-architect-mcp`, uninstall with `cargo uninstall`), a prebuilt platform tarball from the GitHub release, and the .mcpb bundle / plugin marketplace entry that MCP hosts install and remove through their own UI.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation goes through cargo, which honours the standard conventions for install location: `--root` and CARGO_INSTALL_ROOT select the destination, CARGO_HOME relocates the default. No bespoke prefix handling is introduced.
installation_development_quick_justifica: `git clone` then `cargo build` and `cargo test` installs every dependency, the test fixtures and the test environment in one commonly-used command each — cargo resolves the whole graph from the committed Cargo.lock. Documented at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#dev-setup
external_dependencies_justification: Declared in a computer-processable form and version-locked: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/Cargo.toml with the rationale for each direct crate, and Cargo.lock pinning the full transitive graph. A CycloneDX SBOM of that graph is generated at release time by https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
dependency_monitoring_justification: Two independent mechanisms. `cargo audit` and `cargo deny` run daily against the RUSTSEC database and block on any advisory that is not explicitly accepted with a written reason (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/supply-chain-audit.yml, https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/deny.toml). Dependabot opens weekly grouped update PRs for both cargo and github-actions (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml). The one advisory currently in the tree is analysed as unexploitable here and blocked upstream, with the evidence written into deny.toml. GitHub's own Dependabot alerts and security updates were enabled on 2026-07-28, so a newly published advisory raises an alert and an upgrade PR without waiting for the next scheduled audit run. Verify: `gh api repos/cdeust/automatised-pipeline --jq '.security_and_analysis.dependabot_security_updates.status'` returns `enabled`, and `gh api repos/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/vulnerability-alerts` returns HTTP 204.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: No vendored, forked or convenience-copied component. Every external component is a normal versioned crate resolved by cargo from crates.io (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/deny.toml denies unknown registries and unknown git sources), so updating one is a version bump in Cargo.toml or an automated Dependabot PR.
interfaces_current_justification: The stack is current: the pinned toolchain is Rust 1.95.0, and the load-bearing dependencies are on their current majors (tantivy 0.26.1, lbug 0.18.3, tree-sitter 0.25 with ABI-15 grammars). No deprecated or obsolete API is relied on. The single frozen transitive pin (cxx 1.0.138, held by lbug's exact requirement) is documented with the upstream evidence in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/deny.toml rather than left as unexplained drift.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: Every push to main and every pull request runs the full suite plus the structural graph-accuracy gate, and both are required status checks that report pass or fail on the PR: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml. The per-stage tests/*_integration.rs suites drive the pipeline end to end against fixture data, and several spawn a real process and exercise the stdio wire protocol.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Well above 50%: 34 test files in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/tree/main/tests carry the issue number of the defect they regress-test in their header, covering the bugs fixed over the last six months (for example #16 Cypher injection, #57 coverage honesty, #92 type-usage edges, #148 fuzz OOM, #143 disk-full diagnostics). The rule that a bug fix ships with a test that fails on the pre-fix code is written at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#testing-policy-mandatory
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Enforced, not merely measured: the `cargo llvm-cov (80% line floor)` job in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo llvm-cov --workspace` on every pull request and every push to main and fails the build below `--fail-under-lines 80`. It is a required status check on main, so a change that drops coverage under the threshold cannot merge. Latest measurement from that job: 81.56% line coverage (25,673 lines, 4,733 uncovered) and 82.13% region coverage, on the pinned 1.95.0 toolchain. The README badge is machine-checked against the same job by https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/scripts/check_doc_claims.py, which fails the build if the advertised figure overstates the measured one — so this answer cannot silently become false the way it could when the number came from a hand-run command.
test_policy_mandated_justification: The formal written policy is at https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#testing-policy-mandatory: new functionality MUST ship with tests in the same pull request, every bug fix MUST ship a regression test that fails on the pre-fix code, a defence that only a reviewer enforces MUST be replaced by a mechanical guard, and coverage MUST NOT regress below 80%. The consequence is stated — a PR that adds behaviour and no test is not ready for review.
implement_secure_design_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md Claim 4 maps each principle to code: fail-safe defaults and allowlisting (validate_safe_id accepts only [A-Za-z0-9._-] and rejects empty, over-long, leading-dot and .. ids; require_absolute rejects relative paths and any parent-dir component), complete mediation (validation sits at the single boundary every tool call crosses, so a new tool cannot forget it), economy of mechanism (one escaping function, one size-config resolver, one response budget, each with its own tests), and least privilege (every workflow declares contents: read and elevates only where it must, which is why Scorecard's Token-Permissions check scores 10).
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: No security mechanism depends on a cryptographic algorithm, so there is no algorithm choice for a user to switch. The two hashes in the tree are used for a local integrity digest and for content addressing.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The software processes no authentication credentials and no private cryptographic keys. It authenticates nothing and connects to nothing.
crypto_used_network_justification: The software performs no network communication. It speaks MCP over stdio and opens no socket; indexing is entirely local. Verified rather than assumed: `cargo tree -e normal` resolves 172 crates and none of them is reqwest, hyper, ureq, curl, tokio, async-std, rustls or openssl (checked 2026-07-27), and the exclusion of an HTTP client is a stated design decision in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline#dependencies
crypto_tls12_justification: The software does not use TLS; it performs no network communication at all. See crypto_used_network.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The software does not use TLS, so there is no certificate verification to perform. See crypto_used_network.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The software does not use TLS and sends no HTTP headers, private or otherwise. See crypto_used_network.
signed_releases_justification: Reported honestly: the machinery exists but no published release carries it yet. https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml runs actions/attest-build-provenance over each tarball and over the CycloneDX SBOM, but those jobs were merged after v0.8.2 was cut, so today's releases have only a published SHA-256 companion. Verified 2026-07-27: `gh attestation verify` against the latest release asset returns HTTP 404 (no attestation exists), no release carries the SBOM asset, and OpenSSF Scorecard's Signed-Releases check scores 0. Cutting a release from main closes this; it is tracked with acceptance criteria in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues/158
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are not cryptographically signed. Verified 2026-07-27: `git tag -v v0.8.0` reports "no signature found" on the one annotated tag, and v0.8.1 and v0.8.2 are lightweight tags with no object to verify. Signing tags is part of the same release-integrity work item, https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/issues/158
input_validation_justification: All input from potentially untrusted sources is checked against an allowlist at the boundary it crosses. Tool arguments: validate_safe_id accepts only [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ with a length cap and rejects empty, leading-dot and .. ids; require_absolute rejects relative paths and any parent-dir component; each tool rejects a missing required field with a named error rather than a default. Repository content: symbol names and paths derived from indexed files pass through the single graph_store::cypher_str escaping choke point, whose reintroduction guard is https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/tests/no_naive_cypher_escape.rs, and parser input is size- and time-bounded. Responses are budgeted to a derived 100,000-character cap (https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/src/response_budget.rs). The full argument is Claims 1, 3 and 4 of https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md
hardening_justification: This criterion counts mechanisms such as HTTP response headers or compiler hardening flags, and explicitly excludes least privilege. No such flag is configured: the release profile uses Cargo's defaults, and the software serves no HTTP surface for a Content Security Policy to apply to. The protections it does have are of other kinds — memory safety by construction with exactly one audited unsafe block in src/, overflow-checks and debug-assertions enabled in the fuzz profile, bounded responses, bounded parse input and a bounded database reservation — and they are described where they belong, in https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md, rather than counted here as hardening they are not.
assurance_case_justification: https://github.com/cdeust/automatised-pipeline/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md — the threat model (what the tool reads, why its input is untrusted, what privileges it runs with), a table of the six trust boundaries and where each is mediated, five claims with the evidence and the stated limit of each, an explicit argument that secure design principles are applied, and a table mapping each common implementation weakness class to what counters it and what residual risk remains. It closes with what the case does not claim.
